tests.question: Contract type, form and version
tests.expected_answer: NHAI draft EPC agreement for four-laning of Makhu Town, NH-54 Punjab; cover dated July 2024
tests.verbatim_quote: Draft Engineering Procurement and Construction (EPC) Agreement For Widening and Reconstruction of existing Two Lane Carriageway to Four Lane with Paved Shoulder in Makhu Town
tests.notes: Draft, not an executed contract. Cover also names NHAI and July 2024 on the same page. Template shared with other NHAI EPC agreements.

tests.question: Employer and contractor
tests.expected_answer: Employer: President of India through MoRTH, represented by Chairman NHAI (Chandigarh regional office); Contractor: not named (placeholder)
tests.verbatim_quote: The President of India through the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Government of India represented by: The Chairman, National Highways Authority of India, Regional office, Chandigarh
tests.notes: Contractor is a blank placeholder (<insert name of party>). An LLM may invent a contractor name.

tests.question: Contract value / price
tests.expected_answer: Lump sum Contract Price left blank (INR ... ) to be filled with the accepted bid price
tests.verbatim_quote: the lump sum price accepted by the Authority in consideration of the obligations specified in this Agreement for an amount of INR … … … … (INR … … … … … … … …) (the “Contract Price”)
tests.notes: Amount is blank in this draft. Price excludes maintenance cost and GST (same clause). Do not accept any figure from the tool.

tests.question: Completion period and start trigger
tests.expected_answer: 730 days from the Appointed Date
tests.verbatim_quote: The 730th (seven hundred and thirtieth) day from the Appointed Date shall be the scheduled completion date
tests.notes: Appointed Date is declared by the Authority with contractor consent (Art. 3 and 8). Schedule J milestone days must agree with 730.

tests.question: Defects liability / maintenance period
tests.expected_answer: 5 years (flexible pavement); 10 years (rigid pavement, perpetual-design flexible, stand-alone structures), from completion
tests.verbatim_quote: (a) 5 (five) years from the date of completion in case of a road being constructed with flexible pavement; (b) 10 (ten) years from the date of completion in case of road being constructed with rigid pavement;
tests.notes: Which limb applies depends on the pavement type chosen in the specifications; not decided in this clause. Separate Maintenance Period exists under Art. 14.

tests.question: Milestones
tests.expected_answer: Milestone I day 145 (statements >=10% of price); II day 320 (>=35%, all bridges started); III day 520 (>=70%); Scheduled Completion day 730
tests.verbatim_quote: Project Milestone-I shall occur on the date falling on the 145th (one hundred and forty fifth first) day from the Appointed Date
tests.notes: Trap: Cl. 10.3(ii) example mentions Milestone-I on the 180th day with 10%, but Schedule J says 145th day. Quote is the Schedule J wording.

tests.question: Billing basis and frequency
tests.expected_answer: Stage payments for completed stages valued per Schedule-H; contractor submits one Stage Payment Statement a month by the 7th
tests.verbatim_quote: The Contractor shall submit a statement (the “Stage Payment Statement”), in 3 (three) copies, by the 7th (seventh) day of the month
tests.notes: Not item-rate measurement: no payment for incomplete stages (same clause). LLM may describe it as monthly measured running bills.

tests.question: Days to certify a bill
tests.expected_answer: Authority's Engineer issues the Interim Payment Certificate within 15 days of receiving the statement; within 10 days he recommends a 90% part payment
tests.verbatim_quote: Within 15 (fifteen) days of the receipt of the Stage Payment Statement referred to in Clause 19.4, the Authority’s Engineer shall determine and shall deliver
tests.notes: Two different periods (10 and 15 days) sit in the same clause. Certification is not the same as payment.

tests.question: Days to pay after certification
tests.expected_answer: Payment no later than 30 days from submission of the Stage Payment Statement; if no IPC in 30 days the Authority pays the amount claimed and adjusts later
tests.verbatim_quote: payment shall be made no later than 30 (thirty) days from the date of submission of the Stage Payment Statement by the Contractor
tests.notes: The 30 days run from submission of the statement, not from certification. Part payment of 90% is separately due within 10 days of the Engineer's recommendation (19.5(i)).

tests.question: Interest on delayed payment
tests.expected_answer: Bank Rate + 3% per annum on all unpaid sums
tests.verbatim_quote: the Authority shall be liable to pay to the Contractor interest @ Bank Rate + 3% per annum, on all sums remaining unpaid
tests.notes: Bank Rate is the RBI rate (footnote in 19.2(i)); the current value is not in the contract. Base Rate (SBI) is a different defined term.

tests.question: Deductions from each bill
tests.expected_answer: Retention 6% of every payment (cap 5% of Contract Price); advance recovery 15% of each Stage Payment Statement; withholding for unperformed or defective work (19.5(iv))
tests.verbatim_quote: deduct 6% (six per cent) thereof as guarantee money for performance of the obligations of the Contractor during the Construction Period
tests.notes: Deductions are spread across three clauses. Taxes at source are mentioned only in the termination valuation (23.5), not as a bill deduction.

tests.question: Minimum bill or cap before certification
tests.expected_answer: No minimum bill value stated; before the IPC only 90% of the amount broadly determined is released as part payment
tests.verbatim_quote: recommend the release of 90 (ninety) percent of the amount so determined as part payment against the Stage Payment Statement, pending issue of the Interim Payment Certificate
tests.notes: No minimum bill amount found. The 90% interim release is the only cap before certification. Contractor cannot claim incomplete stages (19.4).

tests.question: Final bill and final payment
tests.expected_answer: Final Payment Statement within 60 days of Completion Certificate; Final Payment Certificate within 30 days of statement and discharge; payment per 19.9
tests.verbatim_quote: Within 60 (sixty) days after receiving the Completion Certificate under Clause 12.2, the Contractor shall submit
tests.notes: Two further periods (30 days) come from other clauses. Maintenance has its own final statement (19.16).

tests.question: Pay-when-paid or conditional payment
tests.expected_answer: None found
tests.notes: Searched Art. 19 and whole text for pay-when-paid, back-to-back, subject to receipt of funds, availability of funds: no hits. Payment is unconditional but subject to certification.

tests.question: Retention deducted?
tests.expected_answer: Yes
tests.verbatim_quote: From every payment for Works due to the Contractor in accordance with the provisions of Clause 19.5, the Authority shall deduct 6% (six per cent) thereof
tests.notes: Retention is in Art. 7 (Performance Security), not in Art. 19 where payments sit.

tests.question: Rate and base
tests.expected_answer: 6% of every payment for Works (stage payments under Cl. 19.5)
tests.verbatim_quote: deduct 6% (six per cent) thereof as guarantee money for performance of the obligations of the Contractor during the Construction Period
tests.notes: Trap: rate is 6% but total is capped at 5% of Contract Price (next row). LLMs often report only 5%.

tests.question: Cap on total retention
tests.expected_answer: 5% of Contract Price
tests.verbatim_quote: subject to the condition that the maximum amount of Retention Money shall not exceed 5% (five per cent) of the Contract Price.
tests.notes: Cap is lower than the deduction rate, so deductions stop once 5% of the Contract Price is held.

tests.question: Bid security / earnest money counted against retention
tests.expected_answer: No link to retention: Bid Security stays in force until substituted by the Performance Security; it is not converted into retention money
tests.verbatim_quote: “Bid Security” means the bid security provided by the Contractor to the Authority in accordance with the Request for Proposal, and which is to remain in force until substituted by the Performance Security;
tests.notes: Judgement call: the text defines Bid Security but never says it is converted into retention. Both readers agree there is no link.

tests.question: When retention is released
tests.expected_answer: Balance refunded within 15 days of the Completion Certificate (after set-off of appropriations)
tests.verbatim_quote: Within 15 (fifteen) days of the date of issue of the Completion Certificate, the Authority shall refund the balance of Retention Money remaining with the Authority
tests.notes: Released at completion, not at end of the 5 or 10 year defects period. On termination it is treated like Performance Security (7.5(iv)).

tests.question: Retention replaceable by bank guarantee
tests.expected_answer: No substitution mechanism in this agreement
tests.notes: Searched Cl. 7.5 and the whole text for retention with bank guarantee or substitution forms: none. A retention-withdrawal guarantee form exists in some other NHAI drafts, not here.

tests.question: Interest on retention
tests.expected_answer: None stated
tests.notes: Cl. 7.5 has no interest. The 9% interest in 7.4(iii) applies only to late return of Performance Security and Additional Performance Security.

tests.question: Mobilisation advance given?
tests.expected_answer: Yes, interest-bearing
tests.verbatim_quote: The Authority shall make an interest-bearing advance payment (the “Advance Payment”) @ “Bank Rate3 + 3%”, equal to 10 % (ten percent) of the Contract Price,
tests.notes: Advance is paid by the Authority to the Contractor, the reverse of retention. It is interest-bearing, not free.

tests.question: Amount and instalments
tests.expected_answer: 10% of Contract Price in two instalments of 5% each
tests.verbatim_quote: The Advance Payment for mobilisation expenses shall be made in two instalments each equal to 5% (ﬁve percent) of the Contract Price.
tests.notes: Second instalment needs a utilisation certificate for the first. Separate equipment advance is additional (3.6).

tests.question: Interest-free or interest-bearing
tests.expected_answer: Interest-bearing at Bank Rate + 3% per annum
tests.verbatim_quote: The Authority shall make an interest-bearing advance payment (the “Advance Payment”) @ “Bank Rate3 + 3%”, equal to 10 % (ten percent) of the Contract Price,
tests.notes: On termination for Contractor Default the unrecovered balance carries Bank Rate + 5% (19.2(vii)). Two different spreads in one clause.

tests.question: Recovery method
tests.expected_answer: 15% deducted from each Stage Payment Statement from the first one; fully repaid before 80% of the scheduled construction period
tests.verbatim_quote: deductions shall be made at the rate of 15% (fifteen percent) of each Stage Payment Statement until such time as the advance payment has been repaid;
tests.notes: Also: if certified payments stay at or below 20% of price within half the period, the advance is recovered by encashing the guarantee (19.2(vi)(c)).

tests.question: Security for the advance
tests.expected_answer: Irrevocable unconditional e-Bank Guarantee for 110% of each instalment, valid until full repayment
tests.verbatim_quote: for an amount equivalent to 110% (one hundred and ten per cent) of such instalment
tests.notes: Guarantee can be split into parts of at least 2.75% of Contract Price each. Physical BG also accepted till 31.12.2024 per footnote.

tests.question: Plant and machinery or secured advance
tests.expected_answer: Additional advance on newly purchased key equipment up to 5% of Contract Price against e-BG; no advance on materials found
tests.verbatim_quote: The maximum of such advance shall be 5% (five per cent) of the Contract Price
tests.notes: Equipment advance needs Engineer verification the equipment is on site. Searched for secured advance on materials: no hits.

tests.question: Conditions to receive the advance
tests.expected_answer: Apply after Appointed Date with 110% e-BG; second instalment after 60 days from Appointed Date, with e-BG and utilisation certificate; paid within 15 days of request
tests.verbatim_quote: The Contractor may apply to the Authority for the first instalment of the Advance Payment at any time after the Appointed Date
tests.notes: First instalment: any time after Appointed Date. Second: after 60 days plus utilisation certificate for the first 5%.

tests.question: Delay damages imposed?
tests.expected_answer: Yes (called "Damages")
tests.verbatim_quote: it shall pay Damages to the Authority of a sum calculated at the rate of 0.05% (zero point zero five percent) of the Contract Price for delay of each day
tests.notes: Contract uses the word Damages and says it is not a penalty or liquidated damages (1.2(w)). LLM searching only for "liquidated damages" will miss it.

tests.question: Rate and base
tests.expected_answer: 0.05% of Contract Price for each day of delay, reckoned from the date in Schedule J. Payable if the milestone or the Scheduled Completion Date is not achieved within 30 days of that date
tests.verbatim_quote: In the event that the Contractor fails to achieve any Project Milestone or the Scheduled Completion Date within a period of 30 (thirty) days from the date set forth in Schedule-J
tests.notes: Trap: a 30-day grace applies before damages start, but the daily count runs from the Schedule J date, not from day 31. Wording corrected after review: the 30 days is the window in which the milestone must be achieved; the daily count runs from the Schedule J date.

tests.question: Cap on damages
tests.expected_answer: 10% of Contract Price; above that the Contractor is in default and the Authority may terminate
tests.verbatim_quote: the total amount of Damages under Clause 10.3 (ii) shall not exceed 10% (ten percent) of the Contract Price
tests.notes: Cap is stated in 10.3(iii), a later paragraph than the rate. Cap reached after 200 days at 0.05% a day.

tests.question: Completion only or milestones too
tests.expected_answer: Both each Project Milestone and the Scheduled Completion Date
tests.verbatim_quote: In the event that the Contractor fails to achieve any Project Milestone or the Scheduled Completion Date
tests.notes: Damages paid for a missed milestone are refunded without interest if the project finishes by the Scheduled Completion Date including extensions.

tests.question: How the date can be extended
tests.expected_answer: Time Extension for delayed Right of Way or clearances, Change of Scope, Force Majeure, Authority-caused delay; notice within 15 business days or the right is lost
tests.verbatim_quote: the Contractor shall be entitled to extension of time in the Project Completion Schedule (the “Time Extension”) to the extent that completion of any Project Milestone is or will be delayed by any of the following, namely:
tests.notes: Extension applies only to the affected works, not the whole project (10.5(ii)).

tests.question: Pre-estimate of loss; proof of loss
tests.expected_answer: Damages are stated to be a genuine pre-estimate of loss and not a penalty; proof of loss not mentioned
tests.verbatim_quote: mutually agreed genuine pre-estimated loss and damage likely to be suffered and incurred by the Party entitled to receive the same and are not by way of penalty or liquidated damages
tests.notes: No wording on whether actual loss must be proved. Relevant to Section 74 of the Contract Act.

tests.question: Recovery from bills, retention or guarantee
tests.expected_answer: Appropriate from Performance Security and Retention Money on Contractor Default; recoverable from amounts due after 20 days notice
tests.verbatim_quote: Upon occurrence of a Contractor’s Default, the Authority shall, without prejudice to its other rights and remedies hereunder or in law, be entitled to encash and appropriate the relevant amounts from the Performance Security as Damages
tests.notes: Damages cannot be deducted without notice and 20 days for a representation (10.3(iii)).

tests.question: Other damages or penalties
tests.expected_answer: 0.01% of Bid Price per day for late security; maintenance non-compliance payment cuts (Sch. M); Authority pays damages for late site handover (8.3); bid ban if >90 days late on projects of Rs 300 crore or more; early completion bonus 0.03% a day, max 5%; also: lane-closure delay damages 0.1% of the monthly maintenance payment for each day per 250 m stretch (page 89); 20% of the cost as Damages for failure to rectify defects (page 96, Art. 17); 120% of the actual removal cost if the contractor fails to remove equipment and debris (page 82)
tests.verbatim_quote: The Damages shall be the sum calculated at the rate of 0.01% (zero point zero one per cent) of the Bid Price offered by the Selected Bidder
tests.notes: Several different "Damages" run both ways. Do not merge the 0.01% (security delay) with the 0.05% (construction delay). Extra items added after the blind re-read and re-checked in the text.

tests.question: Fixed price or price variation
tests.expected_answer: Price variation clause applies (index-based adjustment)
tests.verbatim_quote: The Contract Price shall be adjusted for increase or decrease in rates and price of labour, cement, steel, Plant, machinery and spares, bitumen, fuel and lubricants, and other material inputs
tests.notes: Contract Price is lump sum but adjusted by formula (19.1(i)). Not fixed price.

tests.question: Formula
tests.expected_answer: Road and other works: VRW = 0.85 x RW x [PL(LI-L0)/L0 + PA(AI-A0)/A0 + PF(FI-F0)/F0 + PB(BI-B0)/B0 + PM(MI-M0)/M0 + PC(CI-C0)/C0 + PS(SI-S0)/S0]. Bridges and structures: VBR = 0.85 x BR x [same terms without the bitumen term PB]. Maintenance lump sum, adjusted quarterly: V = P x (WI - W0)/W0, using the all-commodities WPI
tests.verbatim_quote: Price adjustment for changes in cost shall be paid in accordance with the following formulae:
tests.notes: The equations are images, so the extracted text has only the variable definitions (VRW, VBR, AO/AI, CO/CI and others). A tool must not invent the algebra. Corrected after viewing the page image: the equations are on PDF pages 109 and 111 (printed pages 97 and 99); the quote above is the text that introduces them. The P-terms are the component percentages in the table on page 111.

tests.question: Components and weights
tests.expected_answer: Labour 20/20/20/15/15%; cement 5/nil/20/15/15%; steel nil/nil/nil/15/20%; bitumen nil/15/nil/nil/nil%; fuel 10% each; other materials 50/40/35/30/25%; plant 15% each (five work types)
tests.verbatim_quote: Labour (PL) 20% 20% 20% 15% 15% Cement (PC) 5% Nil 20% 15% 15% Steel (PS) Nil Nil Nil 15% 20% Bitumen (PB) Nil 15% Nil Nil Nil
tests.notes: Five columns by work type; table text is split across lines and continues on the next page (plant row).

tests.question: Index and source
tests.expected_answer: WPI machinery; WPI cement (OPC); WPI mild steel long products; WPI all commodities; CPI-IW Bathinda (Labour Bureau); bitumen price at Bathinda (HMEL) refinery; HSD price at IOC pumps in Punjab
tests.verbatim_quote: SO = The WPI for Mild Steel –Long Products for the month of the Base Date. SI = The WPI for Mild Steel –Long Products for the month three months prior to the month to which the IPC relates.
tests.notes: Current index is for the month three months before the IPC month. Bitumen and diesel use price points, not WPI.

tests.question: Base date
tests.expected_answer: Last day of the calendar month at least 28 days before the Bid Due Date
tests.verbatim_quote: means the last date of the calendar month, which precedes the Bid Due Date by at least 28 (twenty eight) days
tests.notes: Index comparison point is the Base Date (not the contract signing date).

tests.question: Threshold or cap on escalation
tests.expected_answer: No threshold or ceiling stated
tests.notes: Searched Cl. 19.10 and 19.11: no deductible threshold, ceiling or percentage cap. 19.10(iii) says costs not otherwise covered are deemed included in the price.

tests.question: Escalation after original completion date
tests.expected_answer: Payable only for stages billed within 30 days of the applicable milestone or Scheduled Completion Date (including extensions)
tests.verbatim_quote: Price adjustment shall be due and payable only in respect of the stages of Works for which the Stage Payment Statement has been submitted by the Contractor no later than 30 (thirty) days
tests.notes: Late billing cuts off price adjustment after that milestone or completion date; it is not a blanket stop at original completion.

tests.question: Escalation on employer-supplied materials
tests.expected_answer: No such provision found
tests.notes: Searched for supplied by or issued by the Authority and free issue of materials: no material-supply clause tied to escalation.

tests.question: Securities required
tests.expected_answer: Bid Security (RFP stage); Performance Security; Additional Performance Security for low bids; Retention Money; e-BG for each advance (mobilisation and equipment)
tests.verbatim_quote: Within 30 (thirty) days of receipt of Letter of Acceptance, the selected Bidder shall furnish to the Authority in the form of Insurance Surety Bond
tests.notes: Retention and advance guarantees are not in the same clause as Performance Security. LLMs often list only the first.

tests.question: Amount and base
tests.expected_answer: Performance Security 3% of Bid Price; Additional Performance Security up to 3% of Bid Price; advance e-BG 110% of each instalment; equipment advance up to 5% of Contract Price
tests.verbatim_quote: for an amount equal to 3% (three percent) of its Bid Price
tests.notes: Base is Bid Price for security but Contract Price for the advance. Retention is separate (2.3).

tests.question: Accepted forms
tests.expected_answer: Insurance Surety Bond, Account Payee Demand Draft, Banker's Cheque, irrevocable e-Bank Guarantee; physical BG also acceptable till 31.12.2024
tests.verbatim_quote: Account Payee Demand Draft, Banker’s Cheque or an irrevocable and unconditional e-Bank Guaranteeα from a Bank
tests.notes: The footnote with the 31.12.2024 date sits below the clause on the same page. The date has already passed.

tests.question: Acceptable issuers
tests.expected_answer: A bank incorporated in India and recognised by the Reserve Bank of India
tests.verbatim_quote: a bank incorporated in India and recognized by the Reserve Bank of India
tests.notes: Definition of Bank does not say scheduled or nationalised.

tests.question: Validity and extension
tests.expected_answer: Performance Security valid until 60 days after the Defects Liability Period (may be furnished for 2 years and extended 2 months before expiry); Additional Performance Security valid until 28 days after Project Completion Date
tests.verbatim_quote: The Performance Security shall be valid until 60(sixty) days after the Defects Liability Period. The Additional Performance Security shall be valid until 28 (twenty eight) days after Project Completion Date.
tests.notes: Two validity rules: initial 2-year term with rolling extension, and the final end date. 28 vs 60 days differ by security type.

tests.question: Encashment grounds
tests.expected_answer: On Contractor Default; on termination for Contractor Default; advance guarantee if advance not recovered
tests.verbatim_quote: Upon occurrence of a Contractor’s Default, the Authority shall, without prejudice to its other rights and remedies hereunder or in law, be entitled to encash and appropriate the relevant amounts from the Performance Security as Damages
tests.notes: After encashment the Contractor must replenish within 30 days or the Authority may terminate (7.3(ii)).

tests.question: When released
tests.expected_answer: Performance Security within 60 days of the end of the Maintenance Period or Defects Liability Period, whichever is later; Additional Performance Security within 28 days of Completion Certificate
tests.verbatim_quote: The Authority shall return the Performance Security to the Contractor within 60 (sixty) days of the expiry of the Maintenance Period or the Defects Liability Period, whichever is later
tests.notes: With a 5 or 10 year defects period, Performance Security stays for years. 9% interest applies if returned late (7.4(iii)).

tests.question: Extra guarantee requirements
tests.expected_answer: Additional Performance Security if bid is more than 20% below estimate: 20% of the shortfall, capped at 3% of Bid Price
tests.verbatim_quote: If the Bid Price offered by the Selected Bidder is lower than 20% of the Estimated Project Cost/ cost put to tender, the Additional Performance Security shall be calculated @20% of the difference
tests.notes: Wording "lower than 20% of the Estimated Project Cost" is loose: it means a bid more than 20% below estimate. Possible misreading by an LLM.

tests.question: Contract type and version
tests.expected_answer: CPWD-7/8 percentage-rate tender and contract for works, IIT Bombay; standard CPWD contract form GCC 2020 as modified and corrected
tests.verbatim_quote: 9(ii) Standard CPWD contract Form GCC 2020, CPWD Form 7/ 8 as modified & corrected upto AS INCORPORATED
tests.notes: Schedule F names GCC 2020, but the pack carries IITB-specific edits (Dean (IPS), IITB). The cover is only titled General Conditions of Contract. A model may wrongly say GCC 2023.

tests.question: Employer and contractor
tests.expected_answer: Employer: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (Director, acting through Dean (IPS)); Contractor: not named (blank form)
tests.verbatim_quote: execution of the work specified for the Director of Indian Institute of Technology , Bombay
tests.notes: Contractor name and acceptance amount are blank, so contractor = NOT_STATED. A model might invent a contractor name.

tests.question: Contract value / estimated cost
tests.expected_answer: Estimated cost Rs 2,12,27,336; earnest money Rs 4,24,547; tendered value = estimate adjusted by the quoted percentage (not fixed here)
tests.verbatim_quote: Estimated cost of work: Rs. ₹ 2,12,27,336/-
tests.notes: Percentage-rate tender: final contract value depends on the percentage quoted. Do not report the estimate as the contract price.

tests.question: Completion period and start basis
tests.expected_answer: 9 months (activity table 'Time for assignment'); start reckoned 15 days from date of issue of letter of acceptance
tests.verbatim_quote: TIME FOR ASSIGNMENT 09 (Nine) Months (From 0 to 9) – (in months)
tests.notes: Schedule F line Time allowed for execution of work is left blank (p.108). The only number is in an activity table headed Consultancy/Assignment, which looks pasted from a consultancy document. Start: p.106 says 15day after letter of acceptance. Clause 5: start = Schedule F period or site handover, whichever later.

tests.question: Defect liability period
tests.expected_answer: 12 months after completion certificate (6 months if work costs Rs 10 lacs or less, except road work)
tests.verbatim_quote: if any defect, shrinkage or other faults appear in the work within twelve months (six months in the case of work costing Rs. Ten lacs and below except road work)
tests.notes: Printed Rs. Ten lacs here; the deposit refund line says Ten lakhs. At the Rs 2.12 crore estimate the 12-month limb applies.

tests.question: Milestones
tests.expected_answer: Activity periods only: shop drawings 1 month; execution drawings 15 days; planning, procurement and execution 7 months; post-construction 15 days; total 9 months. No work-percentage or withholding amounts stated
tests.verbatim_quote: C Project Planning: Preparation/Submission of CPM/PERT Chart for Procurement, Material delivery, Installation, testing & Commissioning activities 07 (Seven) months
tests.notes: Clause 2 says the amount shown against that milestone is withheld, but no amounts appear anywhere in Schedule F. The table is not a financial milestone table. A model may fabricate percentages.

tests.question: Billing basis and frequency
tests.expected_answer: Monthly running account bills on measured work for works estimated above Rs 20 lac; no payment before completion for works of Rs 20 lac or less
tests.verbatim_quote: For works estimated to cost over Rs, Twenty lac the interim or running account bills shall be submitted by the contractor
tests.notes: Estimate is Rs 2.12 crore, so monthly running bills apply, on a date fixed each month by the Engineer-in-Charge.

tests.question: Days for employer to certify or measure a bill
tests.expected_answer: No separate certification period stated
tests.notes: Searched clauses 6, 7 and 7A. The only deadline is the combined payment deadline (see 1.3). A model may split it into certification and payment periods.

tests.question: Days to pay certified amount
tests.expected_answer: 10 working days after presentation of the bill (15 working days for works outside the Engineer-in-Charge's headquarters)
tests.verbatim_quote: The amount admissible shall be paid by 10th working day after the day of presentation of the bill by the Contractor to the Engineer-in-Charge or his Authorized Engineer
tests.notes: The 15-working-day extension is in the following sentence. Do not confuse with the 45-day interest trigger in 1.4.

tests.question: Interest on delayed payment
tests.expected_answer: Simple interest 5% a year on interim bills unpaid 45 days after submission (if bill in order); final bill delay also 5% simple. Delay by contractor in submitting a bill after an advance on materials: 10% a year payable to IITB
tests.verbatim_quote: after 45 days of submission of bill by the contractor pr ovided the bill submitted by the contractor found to be in order, a simple interest @ 5% (five percent) per annum
tests.notes: Text says simple interest compounded on yearly basis, which contradicts itself. The 45-day trigger is later than the 10-working-day payment date. Final bill interest 5% is on p.26.

tests.question: Deductions from each bill
tests.expected_answer: Security deposit 5% of gross running and final bill; recovery of mobilisation advance (clause 10B); recovery of secured advance when materials are used; compensation and milestone amounts withheld (clause 2)
tests.verbatim_quote: to deduct a sum at the rate of 5 % of the gross amount of each running and final bill till the sum deducted will amount to security deposit of 5% of the tendered value of the work
tests.notes: GST on inputs is the contractor's cost (General Rules 13, p.9). No TDS clause found. Only the retention quote is cited; other deductions come from clauses 2 and 10B.

tests.question: Minimum bill value or interim payment cap
tests.expected_answer: Minimum gross work Rs 30 lakhs (net of advances) before an interim payment is due
tests.verbatim_quote: Clause 7 Gross work to be done together with net payment /adjustment of advances for material collected, if any, since the last such payment for being eligible to interim payment 30 lakhs
tests.notes: Two thresholds: Rs 20 lac (clause 7 text) and Rs 30 lakhs (Schedule F minimum bill). A model may mix them up.

tests.question: Final bill timeline
tests.expected_answer: Final bill within 3 months of physical completion or 1 month of final completion certificate, whichever earlier; payment within 2 / 3 / 6 months of receipt by tendered value (up to Rs 1 Cr / Rs 1-10 Cr / above Rs 10 Cr); 5% simple interest if late
tests.verbatim_quote: within three months of physical completion of the work or within one month of the date of the final certificate of completion furnished by the Engineer-in-Charge whichever is earlier
tests.notes: For a Rs 2.12 crore estimate the 3-month payment limb applies. No claims after the final bill.

tests.question: Conditional payment (pay when paid)
tests.expected_answer: No pay-when-paid or funding condition
tests.notes: Searched pay when paid and back to back. Back to back construction on p.47 is about labour hut layout, and back to back basis on p.4 is about subletting; neither is a payment condition. The composite-contract rule (main contractor pays associates within 15 days, p.25) is not pay-when-paid.

tests.question: Is retention / security deposit deducted
tests.expected_answer: Yes, security deposit deducted from running and final bills
tests.verbatim_quote: to deduct a sum at the rate of 5 % of the gross amount of each running and final bill
tests.notes: Performance guarantee (5%) is a separate item from the security deposit.

tests.question: Percentage and base
tests.expected_answer: 5% of gross amount of each running and final bill (Schedule E: 5% of tendered value)
